actions.justification: Mandatory first step - obtain complete history including symptom onset, functional class, medication history, and precipitating factors for this HFrEF patient.
Mandatory physical exam to assess for signs of congestion (JVD, crackles, edema), hemodynamic status, and volume overload in this HFrEF patient with EF <40%.
Mandatory ECG to evaluate for arrhythmias, conduction abnormalities (LBBB for CRT candidacy), ischemia, or other precipitating causes in HFrEF patient.
Mandatory workup for HFrEF: assess renal function, electrolytes (Na, K, Cr) to guide therapy and identify contributing factors.
Mandatory for HFrEF evaluation: BNP/NT-proBNP quantifies degree of heart failure, guides management, and establishes baseline for monitoring response to therapy.
Mandatory lab: evaluate for anemia (common HF precipitant/comorbidity) and infection that may worsen cardiac function.
Mandatory action - chest X-ray is required to assess for pulmonary congestion, cardiomegaly, and pleural effusions in this HFrEF patient. Must be completed within 60 minutes.

Mandatory action - TSH is required to evaluate for thyroid dysfunction as a reversible cause or exacerbating factor in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Must be completed within 60 minutes.

Assessing hemodynamic profile (warm/cold, wet/dry) is essential in HFrEF to guide appropriate therapy selection, including diuretics, vasodilators, or inotropes based on perfusion and congestion status.
Patient has HFrEF with EF below 40%. Assessing LVEF is essential to guide therapy optimization, including GDMT decisions and device therapy candidacy.
Patient has HFrEF with EF <40%. ICD assessment is indicated per guidelines for primary prevention of sudden cardiac death in patients with reduced EF on optimal medical therapy.
With HFrEF and EF below 40%, CRT candidacy should be evaluated based on QRS duration/morphology and NYHA functional class per heart failure guidelines.

Patient has HFrEF with EF below 40%. NYHA functional class assessment is essential to guide pharmacological therapy optimization (e.g., beta-blocker titration, ACEi/ARB/ARNI dosing) and determine candidacy for device therapies or advanced interventions.
Evaluating for structural abnormalities (e.g., valvular disease, LV geometry) is important in HFrEF to identify reversible or correctable causes and guide further management decisions.

With confirmed HFrEF and EF <40%, assessing candidacy for advanced therapies (LVAD, cardiac transplantation) is part of comprehensive HF management, particularly if the patient has refractory symptoms or is at high risk.
Patient has HFrEF with EF <40%. Need to verify whether patient is on optimal GDMT (ACEi/ARB/ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i) and for how long, to guide further therapy decisions.

Patient with HFrEF and HR of 80 bpm - if patient is in sinus rhythm and on maximally tolerated beta-blocker with HR still ≥70 bpm, ivabradine is indicated per HFrEF guidelines to reduce hospitalizations.
Cardiac rehabilitation is a Class I recommendation for stable HFrEF patients to improve functional capacity, quality of life, and outcomes.

Patient has HFrEF with EF below 40%. After completing initial workup, confirming optimal GDMT (guideline-directed medical therapy) is the next critical step to ensure the patient is on appropriate evidence-based therapies including ACE inhibitor/ARB/ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, and SGLT2 inhibitor as indicated.

HFrEF with EF<40% is a Class I indication for ACE inhibitor, ARB, or ARNI therapy to reduce mortality and hospitalization. Need to assess if patient is already on this therapy or if it needs to be initiated/optimized.

Beta-blocker therapy is a Class I recommendation for HFrEF with EF<40% (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, or bisoprolol) to reduce mortality. Patient is hemodynamically stable (HR 80, BP 120/80) making initiation or optimization appropriate.

Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (spironolactone/eplerenone) are Class I recommended GDMT for HFrEF with EF<40% to reduce mortality and morbidity. This has not yet been addressed in the completed actions.
Patient with HFrEF may have residual congestion; loop diuretics are standard of care to manage volume overload and improve symptoms in HFrEF.
Advanced therapy candidacy was assessed; initiating comprehensive transplant workup is the next step for a patient with persistent HFrEF EF<40% who may be a candidate for advanced therapies.
